cases.hypothesis: Clause-linking connective or boundary punctuation introducing a following clause.
positive_cues: Semicolon and comma appear at clause boundaries before a new clause.
But and that introduce linked or subordinate clauses.
Each context places the target at a syntactic transition between clauses.
exclusion_cues: Standalone content words that do not connect clauses.
Punctuation or conjunctions used without a following clause transition.

cases.hypothesis: Inflected forms of the verb make expressing causation or creation.
positive_cues: The active forms are made, makes, and make.
Occurrences describe making work good, making someone faithful, making food tastier, or prompting a belief.
exclusion_cues: Other lexical verbs unrelated to making or causing.
Noun uses of make without the repeated verb inflection pattern.

cases.hypothesis: The v or v. separator used in formal legal case citations.
positive_cues: Every active token is v in a party-versus-party legal citation.
Surrounding text is court or appellate case-law prose with citation formatting.
exclusion_cues: Ordinary letter v outside a case citation.
Sports scores or other nonlegal uses of versus abbreviations.

cases.hypothesis: Turkish verb stems or inflectional subword fragments in agglutinative prose.
positive_cues: The repeated target anlam is the Turkish understand stem in truncated phrases.
vermem and erm are Turkish verbal material awaiting or carrying inflectional continuation.
All snippets are Turkish conversational, narrative, or news text.
exclusion_cues: Complete non-Turkish words or nominal fragments without verbal morphology.
Unrelated punctuation or isolated lexical items not embedded in Turkish syntax.

cases.hypothesis: Mojibake or encoding-corrupted CJK character fragments.
positive_cues: Active spans contain visibly garbled CJK-looking sequences and replacement characters.
The surrounding strings show consistent mojibake rather than well-formed natural-language text.
exclusion_cues: Well-formed Chinese, French, or other correctly encoded text.
Plain ASCII tokens without encoding artifacts.
